summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86, down 0.28%, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 1.00% as semiconductors led technology lower for a second straight session ahead of NVIDIA's earnings report Wednesday. The Dow bucked the trend, gaining 0.26% to 53,417.16, as the same defensive rotation held: Consumer Staples added 1.70%, Financials gained 1.29%, and Utilities rose 1.05%, while Technology shed 1.78%. The 10 year yield fell to 4.70%, down 0.72%, as Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond buyback program continued to attract attention, though Stanley Druckenmiller publicly criticized the approach and breakeven inflation rates hit their highest level in more than two months, suggesting bond markets are not entirely buying the deflation story. Gold climbed further to 4,692.10, up 1.11%, Bitcoin held at 79,348.25, up 0.49%, and WTI crude dropped to 82.47, down 2.99%, as the US widened Iran sanctions and Iran vowed retaliation, though oil markets are treating the sanctions as a known risk rather than a shock. The biggest movers were concentrated in the chip and quantum space: MU fell 5.83%, IONQ dropped 8.47%, WDC lost 5.24%, RGTI shed 8.6%, and NVDA declined 2.91% on above average volume. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs Tuesday as Trump threatened 50 percent levies on Canadian autos, keeping the trade war front and center ahead of Core PCE and preliminary GDP on Wednesday and Fed Chair Warsh speaking Friday.
